newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: British buyers renew interest in Dutch flowers.
newsitem.headline: British buyers renew interest in Dutch flowers.

text.p: British buyers are showing renewed interest in purchasing Dutch flowers and plants, a Dutch flower wholesale trade organisation said.

The total value of flowers, plants and related products exported from the Netherlands in August was up seven percent over this time last year, Bedrijfschap voor de groothandel in bloemkwekerijproducten said in its monthly statement.
Bedrijfschap's statement added that the United Kingdom bought 30 percent more flowers with a total value of 33 million Dutch guilders in August.
As well as this, five percent more plants were exported by Dutch growers to the UK, it said.

Germany still topped the list of import nations, with imports growing 8.2 to a total vlaue of 215.4 million guilders, and France took second place with a five percent growth and a total value of 68 million guilders in August.

The Dutch group said British importers are benefiting from an improved economy, and a less fickle domestic currency than in previous years. Good weather had also brought shoppers out into the streets, it stated.
Since the start of this year, British importers have bought flowers and plants with a total value of 274 million guilders, the organisation said.
In total, August exports of flower and plants from the Netherlands to countries around the world had a value of 488 million guilders, Bedrijschap said.
Since the start of the year to the end of August, Dutch growers' exports are up nine percent year-on-year to a total value of 4.8 billion guilders.
